title: Angular resolution: diffraction limit against seeing
caption: An 8 m telescope at 2.2 μm could resolve θ = 1.22λ/D = 0.07″, but turbulence limits it to about 0.6″ unless adaptive optics corrects the wavefront: a gain of about 9×. For comparison the 3 mm pupil of the eye is diffraction-limited at 46″.
alt: A logarithmic scale of angle in arcseconds from 0.01 to 100 with the 8 metre telescope's diffraction limit at 0.07, typical seeing at 0.6 and the eye's diffraction limit at 46.
description: A horizontal logarithmic scale of angular resolution in arcseconds (smaller is sharper).
The 8 m telescope's diffraction limit at 2.2 μm: 1.22 × 2.2 × 10⁻⁶/8 = 3.4 × 10⁻⁷ rad = 0.07″.
Typical seeing without correction: 0.6″, about 9 times worse; adaptive optics recovers most of the difference.
The eye (3 mm pupil, 550 nm): 46″, shown for scale.

claims.name: seeing is about 9 times the diffraction limit
